messages.author: ba3b508d5a663f81
messages.subject: Large gaps in genetic map
parts:
Hi everyone,

I used a double digestion sequencing approach to get SNP markers for 350 progeny (F1 generation). The genome size is 20MB and there are 14 chromosomes. After I removed distorted markers, cosegregating markers, as well as consolidate markers within 500bp of each other, I ended up with about 1119 markers. I attached the map I got from R/qtl using the following code:

est.map(mydata,error.prob=.01,map.function="kosambi",maxit=100000)


I think I have some problems here.
There are many large gaps, most obvious one is on chromosome 7, which has a gap of 46 cM. I checked the markers here and found they do have a large physical distance apart from each other (over 50kb, the average kb per centimorgan is 5kb). I checked recombination frequency myself and did find it is about 40%.
My total cM sizes of chromosomes are over 100, and chromosome 1 is about 200 centimorgans. I am wondering why and how I can improve them. The greatest recombination frequency can only be 50%, so I think I should not have chromosomes which are as big as 200cM.

Thank you anyone for your suggestions or help.

Sincerely,
Ben Chadwick

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Large gaps in genetic map
parts:
It looks okay to me. recombination fraction < 0.5 doesn't put a limit on the genetic lengths of chromosomes. human female chr 1 is >450 cM.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Large gaps in genetic map
parts:
large estimated recombination fractions with small LOD scores could just be chance variation.

large estimated recombination fractions with large LOD scores could mean you have some markers with swapped alleles. I would look to see what the marker pairs are and try to figure out the cause.

karl
